description: Registry of clause tags for docs that carry stable clause identifiers and normative language. Tags: 'check-exists' — a named, runnable check already guards the clause (check-ref points at it); 'checkable' — a mechanical check can guard the clause but is not built yet (check-ref names the intended check and any interim probe); 'judgment-only' — compliance is a per-change judgment no check can decide (justification says why). Clause identifiers are stable: never renumbered, and a retired identifier stays reserved (listed under 'retired').

clauses.justification: Whether a novel event source records what the user did or what the code did is a per-change design judgment; no check can classify sources that do not exist yet.

clauses.justification: Whether a piece of observed context describes the actions faithfully and is worth recording alongside them is a design judgment per capture feature.
Whether a new field is context or an action-stream entry in disguise is judgment; no check can decide a field's meaning from its shape.
Applying the definition to a novel input class — is it a physical input the user deliberately performed? — is judgment.
Classifying a novel consequence as effect versus action is judgment; no check can classify consequences that do not exist yet.
Choosing what stands in as the proxy for an out-of-visibility action is a per-proxy design judgment.
Which effect is the immediate one in a new proxy's causal chain is judgment; regressions on existing proxies are probed by the scripted-truth corpus.
Known duplicate pairs are suppressed and unit-tested per instance, but at-most-one-proxy for a newly designed proxy is judgment.
Whether a proxy's recorded shape identifies the user action is judgment.

scripts/check-schema-echo.js walks every object subschema of every composed platform's schema — composed in-process from the source layers, never the published copies under schemas/dist/, which lag between releases — and holds each to the posture its class states: action objects declare no additionalProperties, the user-defined metadata maps declare a typed-value additionalProperties schema, the discriminating oneOf hosts declare none, and every other object declares additionalProperties: false. No exemption is taken by name alone: a def registered as a discriminating host must still state oneOf members, the action wrapper's members and the defs carrying the action prefix are diffed both ways, and each metadata host must reference the one map definition rather than restate it (an inline copy is refused, so the walk judges one definition and not each copy) with that definition's value schema stating what a value may be. A def outside every registered class is judged as a closed object, so it reds unless it declares additionalProperties: false (npm run lint:schema-echo, a step in CI's lint job). Residue: the walk judges an object subschema when it states type object or carries properties and sits under one of the composition keywords the walk descends — a schema written outside that reach goes unjudged rather than red; and the check holds its posture model against the schemas in that direction only — it never reads this clause's sentence, so a change to either side leaves their agreement a review judgment; the prose gloss (that fields may be added in minor versions and consumers should ignore unknown ones), and whether a newly opened object is genuinely an evolution surface, stay review-held too.

scripts/check-extension-surface.js (npm run lint:extension-surface, a step in CI's lint job) reads the worker dispatcher (packages/extension/background/service-worker.js) through the shared comment-safe tokenizer: the one switch over the message type — brace-depth bounded, required to carry a default: arm (presence-checked; the envelope it answers is ERT-2's own verification) — has its case labels diffed both ways against the panel protocol's Types cells, and the module's message-type equality literals are diffed both ways against the capture-path table's types; the two doc enumerations must be disjoint, every cell must be a lone backticked name, and empty parses and anchor failures (a missing or second dispatcher switch, a missing default: arm, a nested dispatcher) fail loudly. Named residue: the equality scan is module-wide and deduplicated, not listener-scoped — the clause's ahead-of-the-switch mechanism and the guards' placement are review-held (token order is not control flow); a dispatch route outside the tokenized shapes (a computed message type, a negated or reversed-operand type test, an equality test on another receiver) is invisible to the scan; a regular-expression literal carrying a brace inside the dispatcher body corrupts the depth bound and reds with a misleading diagnosis (loud, never green); the panel table's sender-side claim (the set the panel sends) is review-held, as is the tables' payload/response prose.

scripts/check-extension-surface.js (npm run lint:extension-surface, a step in CI's lint job) diffs packages/extension/manifest.json's permissions and host_permissions arrays both ways against the backticked names in this doc's Permissions and Host permissions tables (each selected by section and first header cell) — fence-aware, refusing unreadable table rows and every manifest shape outside its model (a document that is not a JSON object, a permission field that is not an array, a non-string entry, and any optional_permissions/optional_host_permissions key present in a shape other than the empty array — the one shape that requests nothing), rather than skipping them, with empty parses failing loudly. Named residue: the tables' rationale prose is review-held; the manifest's resource-exposure bullets (the CSP absence and the empty web_accessible_resources) and the clause's Chrome Web Store privacy-practices half stay judgment-held.

clauses.check-ref: Ordered insertion, the no-id append-at-arrival (an action without a sequence id passes straight through), and the internal-id strip before store/export are pinned by the desktop reorder-buffer unit tests (packages/desktop/tests/unit/reorder-buffer.test.js; npm run test:desktop); the commit flush barrier's drain-and-continue and sentinel-emitted-last by the worker-pool flush tests (packages/desktop/src-tauri/tests/worker_pool_test.rs regression_298_*; npm run test:desktop:rust), and the bounded fan-out's in-place rescue of a wedged worker by the pool's in-module test flush_all_rescues_a_wedged_worker_in_place_and_still_emits_the_sentinel (packages/desktop/src-tauri/src/capture/worker_pool.rs; same command). The backend's own bounded report wait is truthful: an unserved barrier (dead input thread, stalled pump) recovers the held buffers by fallback drain, emits the sentinel after them, and reports fallback_drained — never a success shape — pinned by the windows-provider in-module tests flush_barrier_timeout_recovers_buffers_by_fallback_drain_and_reports_it (the stalled-pump arm) and flush_barrier_dead_thread_fast_fails_to_fallback_without_waiting (the failed-wake fast-fail arm) (packages/desktop/src-tauri/src/capture/windows.rs; npm run test:desktop:rust), with the completion field's wire form pinned by the command-layer serialization test (packages/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs; same command). The frontend's sentinel handling — waiting for the sentinel, a sentinel that arrives before the waiter registers, immediate collection with the ids stripped on a no-active-capture (id 0) report, the rescued-workers warning, the bounded wait's expiry surfaced (the timeout arm), the fallback_drained report surfaced and still collected on its sentinel, and a duplicate sentinel inert — by the commitWithCompleteness and stopWithCompleteness suites driving the real adapter against a mocked commit_barrier and stop_capture (npm run test:desktop). A normal recording commit reaches completeness through the fused stop-path barrier (stop_capture runs the flush barrier and returns its report), not a separate commit_barrier — pinned end-to-end by the desktop integration completeness-barrier regression (npm run test:integration).
The mode split and mixed recordings are pinned by the capture-mode Rust tests and the corpus coordinate session (npm run test:desktop:rust; npm run corpus:check:desktop).

The filters run as one decision, scope_filter_decision in packages/desktop/src-tauri/src/capture/windows.rs, whose verdict cache and Windows lookups are injected so it is exercisable without a live capture session; it delegates the resolvable-window skip and the excluded process's own events to the shared base rule in packages/desktop/src-tauri/src/capture/scroll.rs. That windows module's in-crate unit tests pin it: an_unresolvable_window_is_skipped_whatever_the_other_filters_say for the delegated skip; target_filter_captures_only_the_selected_application and no_target_set_captures_every_application for the target filter, with the_target_filter_settles_an_out_of_target_event_before_any_lookup for its place ahead of the self-capture lookups; self_capture_exclusion_takes_priority_over_the_target_filter for the exclusion outranking a target that names the excluded process, taken together with the exclusion-off case; a_window_owned_by_an_excluded_process_is_excluded for the owned-window ground; the_self_capture_verdict_is_per_process_and_the_first_event_wins for the per-process verdict, from a first-event exclusion and from a first-event keep, each against a later window whose own answer differs; and a_process_the_tree_and_name_grounds_exclude_never_reaches_the_owner_check for the grounds settled before the owner walk. The Input_Thread wiring the hooks call is pinned in the same module: the target-application atomic it reads per event by the_input_thread_adapter_applies_the_target_application_it_reads, and the thread-local verdict cache it backs the decision with by the_input_thread_adapter_records_a_process_verdict_and_then_rides_it, which supplies the real lookups — the process-tree walk and the executable-name read against a PID no live process can hold, and the owner walk against a window handle that sends it through its no-root-owner guard — asserts the verdict they produce is written, and then flips the written verdict to prove a later event rides the record rather than being judged afresh (npm run test:desktop:rust). The grounds are pinned at their own sites too. The base rule is pinned by that scroll module's in-crate tests, by example over the crate's public surface in packages/desktop/src-tauri/tests/windows_capture_test.rs, and as a property in packages/desktop/src-tauri/tests/pid_filter_test.rs, whose PID-0 property draws every shape the exclusion setting can take — each a distinct entry point or a distinct kind of statement, with the in-crate tests and the property suite riding the mutation run's kill set; keep_event_pid_zero_is_always_filtered, keep_event_excluded_pid_is_filtered, and keep_event_no_exclusion_keeps_all assert those same base-rule arms through the Windows filter windows_should_keep_event, so what they hold is its delegation rather than the Windows-only grounds. Of the self-capture grounds, two have pins on their own implementation, both in the windows module: process-tree ancestor recognition by is_descendant_of_self_is_false and is_descendant_of_actual_parent_is_true (the walk's depth bound is not separately asserted), and the executable-name recognition's Docent-binary-name branch by is_webview_process_matches_docent_binary_name, which asserts the positive match against the test binary's own name and so does not distinguish a whole-name match from a substring one (the webview-runtime-name branch is a named gap — no test asserts it). The owned-window ground is pinned only in part: the decision-level case holds that the decision consults it and honours its answer, and the adapter case runs the real walk through its no-root-owner guard, so a regression that made the walk exclude unconditionally reddens. The other direction is a named gap — nothing exercises a walk that wrongly answers not-owned for a genuinely owned window, which is the over-capture case this ground exists to prevent. The target-application command's normalization of 0 and null is pinned by set_target_pid_stores_nonzero_pid, set_target_pid_treats_zero_as_none, and set_target_pid_accepts_none (packages/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs; npm run test:desktop:rust). The toggle's applied-the-moment-it-changes half is pinned by the desktop integration case toggling self-capture calls invoke with correct value (npm run test:integration) — its applied-at-start half is a named gap.

The per-platform flag wiring this clause states is machine-held by scripts/check-verification-inventory.js (npm run lint:verification-inventory, a step in CI's lint job): for each platform it reads that platform's known-diffs baseline (corpus/known-diffs.extension.json, corpus/known-diffs.desktop-windows.json), the active-session slice of the sufficiency lint's committed baseline, and the gate command the root package manifest defines, then holds both flags in both directions — a trigger that has come true while its flag is absent is as red as a flag passed before its trigger, and the flags are checked on the separate axes this clause states. Flag detection is token-exact, so the --lint both gates already pass never reads as --lint-strict. The watch is also held to the tree it watches, so a correct verdict cannot be computed over the wrong files: each gate command's own --platform and --baseline argument values must equal the platform and baseline the check reads for it (as must the --baseline of npm run sufficiency:check, the file the fail-class population comes from), and the platforms corpus/manifest.json carries sessions for are diffed against the watched set both ways — a platform the corpus grows that the watch has not learned reds rather than going unwatched, and a watched platform the catalogue no longer carries reds equally. Every input is guarded before it is believed: a baseline with no keys, or one missing a key for an active session, is a machinery verdict naming the file rather than an emptiness that would demand the flip. Residue: whether a flipped gate then stays green is the comparator's own business, not this watch's, and the whole-file npm run sufficiency:check surface is deliberately unwatched for the grounds the check's header records.

Further legs hold the enumeration itself: scripts/check-verification-inventory.js (npm run lint:verification-inventory, a step in CI's lint job) diffs this clause's class-table field tokens against the comparator's exported class map both ways, and the same unit suite drives every enumerated token through the pass on a crafted envelope and, over the active sessions' truth files on each corpus platform, asserts every field the pass changes is one the map enumerates. The residue is stated to its real scope, and it has two halves, because the two directions fail in different ways. Under-normalization — a per-run-nondeterministic field the classes do not cover — stays review judgment as format growth adds fields, and it fails loudly: the unnormalized field surfaces as a noisy corpus diff, never a silent skip. Over-normalization — normalizeEnvelope reaching a field the classes should not cover — fails the other way, by masking a real difference rather than by noise, and the class map cannot catch it alone: the map is descriptive, so what the pass reaches is what matters and the map and the doc table are obliged to follow it. The two legs above are what bound it: the committed-truths walk catches the pass touching any field the map does not enumerate, wherever an active session's truth carries that field, and the doc-table diff then forces the enumeration that would legitimise it to be stated in this clause where review sees it. The residue is scoped to that walk: a reach into a field no active truth carries is outside its domain, and stays review judgment. The crafted-envelope leg is not the gap — it drives every enumerated token through the pass.
